there are many factors that affect a student’s learning in the tertiary environment, including: the student’s prior experience, motivation, personality, gender, and the student’s learning style, as well as the teaching methods used.
the most important factors that affect students’ learning of programming are the student’s prior knowledge, the student’s attitude, the student’s motivation and the student’s self-efficacy.
there are a number of predictors of student success. The most important of which is the students’ previous exposure to computers.

the fear factor in the learning of programming in tertiary education.
the factors which affect student learning of programming.
the barriers that prevent students learning to program in a tertiary environment, and the teaching methodologies which could assist students to overcome these barriers.

the fear factor is the single biggest barrier to learning programming and the fear factor is caused by the student’s perception of the programming environment as being hostile and intimidating.
there is no one factor that can be identified as a predictor of student success or failure in learning programming, and that there are many factors that can contribute to student success.
the fear factor is a significant barrier to learning programming in a tertiary environment.

the fear factor, which is a combination of anxiety and self-efficacy, has the potential of being the most significant barrier to the student learning programming.
the student’s fear of programming is a major barrier to their success in learning programming.
the students’ fear of failure and the fear of not being able to cope with the programming environment are the main barriers to their learning to program.

the fear factor is a major inhibitor of student learning in the programming domain.

the fear of programming is a real phenomenon and it affects students’ learning of programming in a negative way.
